name: Land's End / Longships
story: The Peal of granite, not the visitor complex, is the true headland. Longships Lighthouse sits on the reef that wrecked ships bound for the Atlantic.
film: Wide from the cliff path looking at Longships.
seek: Compare the present cliff line with a 19th-century OS sheet.

name: Sennen Cove
story: A working cove under Whitesand Bay. Pilchard cellars and a lifeboat house sit against a beach that changes shape in every winter gale.
film: Boats on the slip; dune grass against the bay.
seek: Ask whether the sand has retreated since the last storm season.

name: Nanjizal / Song of the Sea
story: A boulder cove whose sand comes and goes. The granite arch called Song of the Sea is a late cut by the Atlantic.
film: Through the arch toward the horizon.
seek: Is the beach sand or cobble today?

name: Porthgwarra tunnel
story: St Just miners cut the granite tunnel in the 1890s so farmers could haul seaweed. Gwennap Head is where Channel and Atlantic meet.
film: Walk through the tunnel to light.
seek: Find the daymark colours on Gwennap Head.

name: Minack Theatre
story: Rowena Cade carved a theatre into the cliff from the 1930s. Porthcurno below was the shore end of the Eastern Telegraph cables.
film: Stepped granite seats and the bay.
seek: The first cable landed in 1870.

name: Logan Rock, Treen
story: A rocking logan stone. In 1824 a Navy lieutenant dislodged it and was made to pay for its replacement.
film: Headland ramparts and the stone from below.
seek: Can you still see the Iron Age rampart lines?

name: Merry Maidens
story: A near-perfect late-Neolithic / Bronze Age circle. Folklore says girls turned to stone for dancing on the Sabbath.
film: Circle against the sky.
seek: Count the stones. Early accounts do not always agree.

name: Madron Well and baptistery
story: A cloutie well and a ruined baptistery. William Borlase recorded such wells in the 18th century.
film: Cloth on the thorn; stone baptistery in leaf-light.
seek: Read any names on the clouties without touching them.

name: Lanyon Quoit
story: A portal dolmen, once tall enough for a horse and rider. It collapsed in 1815 and was rebuilt lower.
film: Capstone silhouette.
seek: Stand where a rider would no longer pass under.

name: Men-an-Tol
story: Cornish for stone with a hole. It may be a ruined circle, not a single monument.
film: Through the hole to Carn Galva.
seek: Look for fallen stones in the turf.

name: Men Scryfa
story: An inscribed stone to Rialobran, son of Cunoval. The Four Parishes Stone nearby marks Zennor, Morvah, Madron and Gulval.
film: Inscription in side light.
seek: Find the lettering in raking light.

name: Boskednan Nine Maidens
story: A damaged stone circle on the ridge, with Ding Dong mine chimney in the same view.
film: Circle and engine-house together.
seek: Which stones still stand?

name: Carn Euny
story: An Iron Age village of courtyard houses. The fogou is more than 20 metres long.
film: House rings from above; the fogou entrance.
seek: Why build a fogou?

name: Boscawen-un
story: A stone circle with a leaning centre stone, quartz flashing in the ring.
film: Centre stone lean; quartz close-up.
seek: Stand at the centre and see which hills take the horizon.

name: Botallack Crowns
story: Two engine houses on the cliff that drained shafts under the Atlantic. World Heritage mining landscape.
film: Houses against the sea from the coast path.
seek: Which tramway lines are still visible as shelves in the cliff?

name: Levant Mine
story: The only Cornish beam engine still in steam on its original site. In 1919 the man-engine failed and 31 men died.
film: Engine house on the edge.
seek: The 1919 plaque.

name: Geevor
story: Last working tin mine in the west, closed 1990.
film: Headgear and dressing floors; the view to Pendeen Watch.
seek: How late was tin still leaving this cove?

name: Cape Cornwall
story: England's only cape. The chimney is from Cape Cornwall Mine (1836-79). Two seas meet here.
film: Chimney and the Brisons; Priest's Cove boats.
seek: Why is it a cape and Land's End is not?

name: Ballowall Barrow
story: A huge entrance grave above the cliff, cleared in the 19th century.
film: Barrow chambers and the sea.
seek: How many chambers can you still read in the plan?

name: Carn Kenidjack
story: The Hooting Cairn. Tregeseal stone circle lies below.
film: Summit granite; circle on the common.
seek: Listen at dusk.

name: Chun Quoit and Castle
story: A well-preserved Neolithic quoit beside an Iron Age hillfort.
film: Quoit capstone; rampart bank.
seek: Which hedge lines look prehistoric, and which are mining?

name: St Just plain-an-gwarry
story: A medieval playing place for Cornish-language drama, still a green in the town.
film: The circular green; granite town streets.
seek: When was the last miracle play spoken here?

name: Porth Nanven
story: The Dinosaur Egg beach: rounded granite cobbles, a raised beach from a higher sea.
film: Cobbles and the low sun.
seek: The raised beach is a former shoreline. How high was the sea?

name: Zennor mermaid
story: The church pew shows a mermaid who, they say, lured Matthew Trewhella to Pendour Cove.
film: Bench-end carving; church and moor.
seek: Walk a piece of the Coffin Path.

name: Gurnard's Head
story: A cliff castle on a head that looks like the fish. Iron Age banks still cut the neck.
film: Ramparts from the neck; zawn and stack.
seek: How many lines of bank can you still walk?

name: Pendeen Watch
story: Lighthouse of 1900, after wrecks on this north coast.
film: Lantern and Geevor together.
seek: Which wrecks forced the light to be built?
